name: Osmocom Docker Playground
what_it_is: A collection of 126+ Docker containers and test automation infrastructure for the Osmocom cellular telecommunications stack. Primarily used to run TTCN3 testsuites that validate GSM/UMTS core network components (BSC, MSC, HLR, MGW, GGSN, etc.) against their protocol interfaces.
measurement: bpftrace script execution for performance profiling (enabled via RUN_BPFTRACE env var)
gdb integration for crash diagnostics with backtrace collection
Kernel module functional validation through QEMU-based testing
configuration: IMAGE_SUFFIX: selects stack version (default: master; alternative: latest)
OSMO_TTCN3_BRANCH: specifies test framework git branch
DOCKER_ARGS: pass additional docker runtime arguments
TEST_CONFIGS: select a subset of multi-config test runs
TEST_NAME: run a single isolated test case
RUN_BPFTRACE: enable bpftrace profiling for BTS tests
KERNEL_TEST: enable QEMU-based kernel module validation
KERNEL_REMOTE_NAME / KERNEL_URL / KERNEL_BRANCH: kernel git source
modes: kernel module testing: userspace vs. kernel-based GTP-U via QEMU
single test execution: individual TTCN3 test case isolation via TEST_NAME
constraints: TTCN3 testsuites are being migrated; historical suites being relocated to osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git, so suite locations may shift
Kernel module testing (QEMU path) is practical only for OsmoGGSN; not generalised across all components
Supported base OS images are Debian (stretch through trixie/sid) and CentOS 7/8; platform-specific Dockerfiles required for each
No real radio hardware is included; all air-interface testing is emulated or stub-based
HTTP-based source staleness detection for layer caching means stale builds are possible if upstream packages change without a content-length change
docker_services: debian-bookworm-build, debian-bullseye-build, debian-buster-build, debian-trixie-build, debian-sid-build (base build images)
ttcn3-bsc-test, ttcn3-bts-test, ttcn3-hlr-test, ttcn3-mgw-test, ttcn3-msc-test, ttcn3-pcu-test, ttcn3-stp-test, ttcn3-ns-test
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml at repository root; orchestration is done via individual jenkins.sh scripts and docker_images_require declarations
No fault injection or traffic impairment tooling (no tc/netem wrappers, no packet loss simulation)
No persistent metrics storage or time-series database (no Prometheus, Grafana, etc.)
No documented REST/gRPC API surface for programmatic control
No security scanning or vulnerability assessment tooling
No real radio hardware support — air-interface is fully emulated
